Article Title: J&K cop accused of sexually exploiting constable gets bail from HC
Article Text:
Kotwal was booked under multiple BNS sections after a departmental inquiry

SRINAGAR: The J&K high court has granted anticipatory bail to a police sub-inspector accused of sexually exploiting a woman constable on the false promises of marriage, observing that prima facie, the relationship appeared to be consensual.The constable had alleged that the SI, Vikrant Kotwal, deliberately concealed his marital status to trap her into a relationship after they came in contact in Sept 2024 while posted at Samba police station. He repeatedly promised to marry her in order to continue the sexual relationship even as he persuaded her to terminate two pregnancies, and abandoned her after she became pregnant a third time, she alleged.Kotwal was booked under multiple BNS sections after a departmental inquiry, carried out on the constable’s complaint, recommended a proper investigation.Kotwal moved HC after the court of principal sessions judge in Jammu’s Samba district dismissed his anticipatory bail plea on July 23.In his order, Justice Sanjay Dhar said considering their prolonged relationship, especially even after the woman discovered that the SI was married and had children, it “would be inconceivable that the same would not be consensual in nature”.
Article Summary: The J&K high court has granted anticipatory bail to a police sub-inspector accused of sexually exploiting a woman constable on the false promises of marriage. The constable had alleged that the SI, Vikrant Kotwal, deliberately concealed his marital status to trap her into a relationship.

Article Title: ECI schedules September 17 hearing with rebel TMC delegation over party representation
Article Text:
Election Commission of India

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has scheduled a hearing with a five-member delegation led by Ritabrata Banerjee on September 17 in connection with representations received by the poll panel concerning the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC).In a letter dated September 16, the Commission said the hearing will be held at 3 pm at Nirvachan Sadan, Ashoka Road, New Delhi.ECI wrote the letter with the subject, "Representations received in the Commission with respect to All India Trinamool Congress, a recognised political party in the States of West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura – Reg."The communication referred to the ECI's earlier letter dated September 12 and asked Banerjee to provide the names of the five delegation members along with their vehicle details to election@eci.gov.in for necessary arrangements.The hearing comes amid the ongoing dispute between rival TMC factions over the party's organisational control, name and election symbol.
Article Summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has scheduled a hearing with a five- member delegation led by Ritabrata Banerjee. The hearing comes amid the ongoing dispute between rival TMC factions over the party's organisational control, name and election symbol.

Article Title: Chhattisgarh Maoist attack: 10 convicts sentenced to death 13 years after massacre
Article Text:
NIA court on Wednesday sentenced all 10 convicts to death

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than 13 years after the 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack in Chhattisgarh, an NIA court on Wednesday sentenced all 10 convicts to death in the case, in which 29 people were killed.Earlier this month, special NIA court judge Abhay Singh Rajput in Jagdalpur convicted all 10 accused, including two women, who were facing trial in the case, defence lawyer Arvind Choudhary said.The attack, one of the deadliest incidents of violence linked to Left Wing Extremism, took place on May 25, 2013, when Maoists ambushed the Congress' 'Parivartan Rally' on a national highway in Jhiram Valley under Darbha police station limits in Bastar district.Twenty-nine people, including Congress leaders, civilians and security personnel, were killed and more than 30 others injured in the attack, which virtually wiped out the party's top leadership in the state at the time.Those killed included then-state Congress chief Nand Kumar Patel and his son Dinesh, former Leader of Opposition in the Assembly Mahendra Karma, former Union minister Vidya Charan Shukla, and senior Congress leader and former MLA Uday Mudliyar.
Article Summary: The attack took place on May 25, 2013, when Maoists ambushed the Congress' 'Parivartan Rally' on a national highway in Jhiram Valley. 29 people, including Congress leaders, civilians and security personnel, were killed and more than 30 others injured.

Article Title: 'Faced them as freedom fighter faced bullets': TMC MP Mahua Moitra after eggs pelted at her
Article Text:
Moitra claims that BJP workers pelted eggs at her

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Wednesday claimed that BJP workers pelted eggs at her in her constituency in West Bengal, and took a dig at Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Datta over his earlier remarks on her.Moitra shared a video on X in which she appeared to have been hit by eggs. Referring to Justice Datta’s earlier comments, she wrote: “Big shout out to Hon’ble Justice Dipankar Datta ! MiLord - I came to my constituency for a meeting informing West Bengal police & BJP workers with their help pelted eggs on me. True to your advice I faced them as a freedom fighter faced bullets.”The Supreme Court had earlier refused to entertain Moitra’s plea challenging a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police in a hate speech case.During the hearing, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, told the bench that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually.He said Moitra had faced threats of eggs being thrown at her during an earlier visit to the police station and that eggs were later actually thrown.The bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu declined to interfere with the high court’s direction asking Moitra, the Krishnanagar MP, to join the investigation.“You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest?” the bench observed, according to news agency PTI.The bench also said, “These are applications that should not come before this court at all.”Moitra’s counsel subsequently withdrew the petition after the bench indicated that it would not grant relief. The petition was then dismissed as withdrawn.
Article Summary: Mahua Moitra claims that BJP workers pelted eggs at her in her constituency in West Bengal. She took a dig at Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Datta over his earlier remarks on her. The Supreme Court had earlier refused to entertain Mo it’s plea challenging a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police in a hate speech case.

Article Title: Thousands of devotees witness Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple consecration ceremony in Madurai
Article Text:
Thousands of devotees attended the grand consecration ceremony at Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple.





MADURAI: Thousands of devotees thronged Madurai on Thursday to witness the consecration ceremony of Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple which was conducted in a grand manner after 17 years. The previous consecration ceremony of the temple was conducted in 2009.The consecration ceremony was performed between 7.40am and 8.10am on Thursday amid chanting of Tamil and Sanskrit hymns. Following poojas, theertham (holy water) was poured on the kalasams atop the temple towers. Theertha was sprayed on the devotees using pipes and drones.The main yaga sala rituals for the consecration of the Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple commenced on September 11. A total of 180 yaga kundams have been set up to perform rituals. The rituals which commenced continued till the consecration ceremony.LED screens were installed in several places around the temple for the devotees to witness the ceremony. Elaborate arrangements were made by the Madurai district administration and Madurai corporation officials by installing drinking water tanks and mobile toilets in various places around the temple. Large number of police personnel were deployed to ensure safety and to regulate the crowd during the event.
Article Summary: The previous consecration ceremony of the temple was conducted in 2009. A total of 180 yaga kundams have been set up to perform rituals. Elaborate arrangements were made by the Madurai district administration and Madurai corporation officials by installing drinking water tanks and mobile toilets.

Article Title: Nigerian national who murdered his friend over a woman in Pune denied bail
Article Text:
A Nigerian national's bail application was rejected by a judge.





PUNE: Additional Sessions Judge S D Kulkarni on Tuesday rejected the bail application of Nigerian national Nnsemeka Maduabuchi Onyia, 48, accused of murdering a compatriot during a late-night altercation in Pisoli in Jan, saying the prosecution had collected sufficient material linking him to the crime and there was a possibility of him fleeing from justice if released.Onyia was arrested on Jan 12 in connection with an FIR registered at Kalepadal police station under sections 103(1) and 3(5) of the BNS, Section 4(25) of the Arms Act and Sections 37(1) and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act. The chargesheet has been filed, though no prosecution witness had been examined when the bail application was decided.The case relates to the death of Yemeka Kristian, 40, who was allegedly assaulted after a dispute during a dinner gathering at a Nigerian woman’s flat in Pisoli in the early hours of Jan 12. Police said the dispute was linked to a romantic relationship involving the woman. Kristian was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic after the assault but died while undergoing treatment. Police had registered a murder case against three Nigerian nationals and arrested Onyia and another accused while the third accused is still at large.The judge noted that the FIR named Onyia as an aggressor and that eyewitnesses allegedly stated that he took a sharp weapon from the kitchen, followed Kristian and assaulted him on vital parts of the body. The court also referred to medical papers showing multiple chop wounds and to the informant’s statement regarding an alleged statement made by Kristian before his death.The judge held that considering the gravity of the offence, the material against Onyia and the possibility of his fleeing to Nigeria, he was not entitled to bail.
Article Summary: Nigerian national Nnsemeka Maduabuchi Onyia, 48, is accused of murdering a compatriot. The case relates to the death of Yemeka Kristian, 40, who was allegedly assaulted after a dispute during a dinner gathering at a Nigerian woman’s flat.

Article Title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s wife files defamation case against Majithia, Harsimrat and Khaira
Article Text:
Gurpreet Kaur has officially lodged a criminal defamation suit against several political figures





CHANDIGARH: Gurpreet Kaur, wife of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann , on Wednesday filed a criminal defamation complaint in a Chandigarh district court against SAD functionaries Bikram Singh Majithia and Harsimrat Kaur Badal and Sukhpal Singh Khaira of Congress for allegedly levelling false allegations against her.The complaint was filed under Sections 210 and 222 of BNSS for offences under Section 356 of BNS and seeks to summon and prosecute the three.Gurpreet Kaur claimed the allegations portrayed her as seeking money to influence the govt machinery to help a rape accused. She said Majithia made the allegations at a Sept 1 Chandigarh press conference, presenting audio recordings, photographs and CCTV footage to claim people close to her were involved in financial transactions.Gurpreet Kaur had earlier issued legal notices demanding apologies within 24 hours, which Khaira publicly tore up while declaring he would face legal action.The complaint follows a separate civil suit Gurpreet Kaur filed against retired Punjab and Haryana high court Judge Ranjit Singh, Majithia and Khaira. In that case, a Chandigarh court on Sept 9 temporarily restrained the three from publishing, circulating or circulating defamatory content about the alleged bribe demand against her until further orders, setting the next hearing on Sept 30.Gurpreet Kaur has denied all the allegations and the criminal court is reviewing her complaint.
Article Summary: Gurpreet Kaur, wife of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann, files criminal defamation complaint against SAD functionaries Bikram Singh Majithia, Harsimrat Kaur Badal and Sukhpal Singh Khaira of Congress. Kaur claims the allegations portrayed her as seeking money to influence the govt machinery.

Article Title: Telangana CM A Revanth Reddy orders probe into land parcels around KCR farmhouse
Article Text:
Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy in the assembly on Wednesday

‘Dharani part-2 irregularities soon’





HYDERABAD: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Wednesday ordered an inquiry into land parcels around former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao’s Erravelli farmhouse, alleging that around 700 acres were under KCR family’s control, including 388 acres of govt land.Speaking in the assembly, Revanth said govt land parcels found around farmhouse limits will be recovered and allotted to eligible poor people, especially Dalits. He said the land parcels on which “purification” was carried out would be used to provide rights to Dalits.Revanth also alleged that members of KCR’s family and relatives held 439 acres across nine districts, 24 mandals and 31 villages. According to figures presented by him, 67 acres land was held by KCR’s family and 123 acres by a senior BRS leader’s family.He also said that 79 acres land was held by one political family, 30 acres by a former minister’s family, while two other families hold 101 acres and 37 acres land.Revanth said KCR and his wife were entitled to hold 27 acres under the rules, but the figures showed them owning 67 acres. He said 123 acres was held in the names of members of another political family, including 49 acres in one person’s name, 17.5 acres in his wife’s name, and 46.3 acres and 9.3 acres in the names of two other relatives.He alleged that Telangana movement and Dharani portal had been used to the accumulate land. Citing an alleged Dharani irregularity, he said 1,389 acres in survey no. 318/A1 in Chinthalapalem mandal of Suryapet district had been entered in the name of just one person.He said after his govt came to power, the land was brought back under govt control and placed on the prohibited list.The CM also alleged that land linked to the Satyam scam was transferred into the names of relatives of a BRS leader and claimed that the farmhouse was located on this land.Revanth further alleged that land worth Rs50 crore was registered for Rs 1.53 crore before an election and questioned how 11.5 acres of inam land parcels became part of a 50-acre farmhouse. He also referred to 650 acres of govt land in another case while alleging large-scale diversion of govt land parcels during the previous govt.Chief minister A Revanth Reddy alleged that a Rs1 lakh crore land scam had taken place in Telangana and said the govt would constitute a SIT into probe it.Speaking in the assembly, Revanth said the entire alleged scam will be brought to light within a month. “So far, what we have revealed is only Dharani part-1.We will soon expose Dharani part-2 irregularities,” he said. Revanth said he wanted BRS members to be present in assembly when the details were disclosed. He also alleged that irregularities involving TGIIC land would be exposed during the budget session. He claimed that thousands of crores of rupees had been siphoned off using the Dharani portal.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry into land parcels around former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao’s Erravelli farmhouse. He alleged that around 700 acres were under KCR family's control, including 388 acres of govt land. Revanth also alleged that members of KCR's family and relatives held 439 acres.

Article Title: Told to remove Tipu Sultan pic from office, Malegaon deputy mayor moves Bombay HC
Article Text:
Malegaon Deputy Mayor challenges an order to remove Tipu Sultan's photograph from her office.





MUMBAI: Deputy mayor of Malegaon Municipal Corporation has petitioned the Bombay high court challenging recent order issued to her by the corporation's secretary to remove a photograph of Tipu Sultan from her office.Shaan E Hind Nihal Ahmed also challenged state's circulars of 2002 and one dated back to September 15, 1965 that set out an approved list of photographs or portraits of 24 national leaders that can be displayed in public offices.Senior counsel Mukesh Vashi appearing for the Dy Mayor said she has displayed photos of 12 national leaders in the chamber she was allotted at the Municipal Corporation building. She received an order on August 27 from the corporation secretary to display only the 24 national leaders approved in the government resolutions followed by an order on August 31 to remove the photo of Tipu Sultan.She also received the copy of a letter addressed by the leader of Opposition, to the Chief Minister objecting to the photo of Tipu Sultan in her chamber. The dy Mayor informed the HC that she replaced the photo with one showing Rani Laxmibai with Tipu Sultan, which was also being objected to.Vashi said the photo of the Sultan of Mysore was also on display in a district court, the Parliament Central Library, Delhi Legislative Assembly and other places.He submitted that there was no objection to photos of other leaders she had displayed whose names were not on the approved list.Vashi said the circulars cited by the State could only be directory, not mandatory. Bhupesh Samant additional govt pleader appearing for the State and Malegaon police opposed the petition on its very maintainability. The HC Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna issued notice and seeking a reply posted the matter after 3 weeks for a hearing
Article Summary: Malegaon Deputy Mayor challenges an order to remove Tipu Sultan's photograph from her office. She received an order on August 27 from the corporation secretary to display only the 24 national leaders approved in the government resolutions. The HC Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna posted the matter after 3 weeks for a hearing.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: Palghar hospital assault case: MLA Rajendra Gavit's son, 9 Govindas arrested
Article Text:
The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.





PALGHAR: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of MLA Rajendra Gavit, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar.9 other Govindas were also arrested in the case. The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations, when local Shiv Sena functionaries allegedly created a ruckus at Relief Hospital over the treatment of injured Govindas.They allegedly assaulted a hospital employee and took away five injured Govindas who were admitted to the ICU.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe and city chief Rahul Gharat.So far, only Gharat had been arrested, while the other accused were absconding. Police had launched a search for them.On Friday, police arrested Rohit Gavit from his residence in Mira Road. According to police, Gavit had obtained a new SIM card and inserted it into his old mobile phone.This helped police trace his location through technical surveillance and arrest him.Police also arrested nine other accused who were among the Govindas involved in the case. They were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded all the accused in police custody till September 13.
Article Summary: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of an MLA, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar. The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations. Police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena chief Kundan Sankhe and Rahul Gharat.

Article Title: Pune YouTuber gets bail in obscene remarks against minister, woman corporator case
Article Text:
Santosh Pandit

Pune:





Additional sessions judge S U Wadgaonkar on Wednesday granted bail to city-based social media activist Santosh Pandit, arrested in connection with allegations of making obscene and sexually suggestive remarks against Maharashtra minister Chandrakant Patil and a woman corporator of Pune Municipal Corporation.The court noted that the offences invoked carried a maximum punishment of three years and held that the prosecution’s remaining efforts to obtain evidence could be undertaken without keeping Pandit in detention.According to the FIR registered at Kothrud police station, a woman (36) had viewed videos uploaded by Pandit on YouTube containing allegedly obscene and sexually suggestive remarks regarding Patil and the woman corporator. The FIR also referred to earlier videos in which similar remarks were allegedly made regarding the chief minister.The prosecution and the informant opposed bail, submitting that Pandit had repeatedly made sexually coloured remarks on social media and that his account remained active. They also cited apprehensions of him influencing or intimidating the complainant and witnesses, besides submitting that the role of other persons and financial transactions required investigation and CDRs were yet to be obtained.The court noted that the uploaded videos and posts were already with the investigating officer. “Whether there was a deliberate intention or it was made in ordinary course will be tested during the course of trial,” the judge observed.Pandit was arrested from his residence in the night intervening Sept 2-3. He was subsequently remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Santosh Pandit was arrested in connection with allegations of making obscene and sexually suggestive remarks against Maharashtra minister Chandrakant Patil and a woman corporator. The court noted that the offences invoked carried a maximum punishment of three years and held that the prosecution’s remaining efforts to obtain evidence could be undertaken without keeping Pandit in detention.

Article Title: Former union minister EM Sudarsana Nachiappan passes away at 79
Article Text:
EM Sudarsana Nachiappan, former Union minister, dies at 79





SIVAGANGA: Senior Congress leader and former Union Minister EM Sudarsana Nachiappan passed away at his residence in Sivaganga district on Thursday following a brief illness. He was 79.A veteran Congressman, Nachiappan began his political journey in 1969 and rose through the ranks of the party over several decades. He served as the Lok Sabha member from Sivaganga between 1999 and 2004 after defeating senior leader P Chidambaram in the parliamentary election. He later represented Tamil Nadu in the Rajya Sabha from 2004 to 2016.Nachiappan held several key positions in Parliament and chaired important committees during his tenure. He served as Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry in the UPA government led by former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh from 2013 to 2014.Born in Eriyur in Sivaganga district, Nachiappan was a lawyer by profession and had practised in the Supreme Court.Political leaders across party lines expressed grief over his demise. Former Union finance minister P Chidambaram expressed his condolences over X post. Congress MP Karti Chidambaram also paid his last respects.MP Kanimozhi, VCK chief Thol Thirumavalavan also expressed their grief and offered condolences to the family of the bereaved over the X post.
Article Summary: EM Sudarsana Nachiappan passed away at his residence in Sivaganga district on Thursday following a brief illness. The veteran Congressman began his political journey in 1969 and rose through the ranks of the party over several decades. He served as Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry in the UPA government led by former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: Six arrested for murdering fellow guest worker in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Coimbatore:





Six guest workers were arrested on Wednesday, in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district on Monday.Chettipalayam police have identified the arrested as Tuithe Reang, 22, Sunil Rai Reang, 24, Kotho Ram Reang, 30, Sumit Kumar, 20, Sramit Trang, 35, and Santhosh Kumar, 20, all from Tripura.The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit near Othakkalmandapam within Chettipalayam police station limits. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.Investigation revealed that the deceased and the accused were working as housekeeping staff in a private college near Othakkalmandapam. On Monday night they had all consumed alcohol together, and an altercation broke out when the accused asked Badal Shit for money to buy more alcohol, and he refused.“During the altercation, the accused beat him, and Badal Shit died of the severe injuries he suffered in the assault. They then buried him and fled,” said an officer.All six were produced before the judicial magistrate and remanded in custody.
Article Summary: Six guest workers were arrested in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district. The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan first to file nomination
Article Text:
K Padmarajan filling his nomination





TIRUPUR: Filing of nominations for the Dharapuram reserved (scheduled caste) assembly bypoll in Tirupur district began at 11am on Wednesday, with self-styled “Election King” K Padmarajan becoming the first candidate to submit papers before revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja. He is contesting as an independent candidatePadmarajan, a tyre shop owner from Attur in Salem district, said this was his 256th nomination since 1988, filed in Tamil Nadu and other states to underline that ordinary citizens could also contest elections. He claimed that the effort was also part of a Guinness record attempt, adding that he had previously contested against leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, former chief ministers J Jayalalithaa, M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He had spent lakhs of rupees on filing nominations over the years.According to the election schedule, nominations can be filed till Sept 16. Scrutiny will be held on Sept 17, and the last date for withdrawal is Sept 19. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.The Dharapuram constituency has been a reserved seat since 1967. The constituency has seen shifting electoral outcomes in recent cycles, with AIADMK winning in 2011, Congress in 2016 and DMK in 2021, before the seat returned to AIADMK in the last assembly election.It is for the first time that a bypoll is going to be held in Tirupur district, which was formed in 2009. The bypoll has been necessitated by the resignation of R Sathyabama, who was the sitting MLA. Sathyabhama, who contested on behalf of AIADMK, won the election from Dharapuram constituency by securing 81,100 votes. She voted in support of the TVK during the floor test in the assembly and subsequently resigned from her MLA post and joined the TVK.Meanwhile, DMK on Wednesday announced S Suganya,33, a lawyer and party women’s wing functionary, as its candidate in the constituency.
Article Summary: Self-styled ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan became the first candidate to submit papers. He said this was his 256th nomination since 1988. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.

Article Title: Man, 50, arrested for sexually harassing speech–impaired girl
Article Text:
Police have arrested a 50-year-old man on charges of sexually harassing a 10-year-old speech-impaired girl in Tirunelveli district.





Tirunelveli: Police have arrested a 50-year-old man on charges of sexually harassing a 10-year-old speech-impaired girl in Tirunelveli district.Police identified the accused as Manthiraraj. The survivor, a Class V student, was his neighbour. The girl’s parents are also speech-impaired. The girl went to provide water to the cow on Monday when Manthiraraj, who was under the influence of alcohol, allegedly harassed the girl, police said.The girl’s mother, who witnessed the incident, intervened and rescued her. She lodged a complaint with Nanguneri police on the same day. Police registered a case under sections 7&8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act and launched an investigation.After a preliminary probe ascertained that the girl was sexually harassed, police arrested Manthiraraj. He was remanded in judicial custody on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Police identified the accused as Manthiraraj. The survivor, a Class V student, was his neighbour. The girl’s mother, who witnessed the incident, intervened and rescued her. Police registered a case under sections 7&8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

Article Title: 3 cops suspended in temple guard custody death case
Article Text:
Three police personnel, including an inspector, were suspended in connection with the custodial death of Ajith Kumar, the 28-year-old temple watchman who allegedly died due to police torture during interrogation





Madurai: Three police personnel, including an inspector, were suspended in connection with the custodial death of Ajith Kumar , the 28-year-old temple watchman who allegedly died due to police torture during interrogation in Sivaganga district.Sivaganga superintendent of police Abishek Gupta ordered suspensions of Thirupuvanam inspector Ramesh Kumar, sub-inspector Sivakumar and head constable Ilaiyaraja. In an additional chargesheet filed recently, CBI named the three of them also as accused apart from then Manamadurai DSP Shanmugasundaram, who was subsequently suspended. Following a court order, all four were remanded last week.The CBI, which took over the investigation, initially registered murder cases against six special force personnel who were subsequently arrested and remanded to judicial custody.Ajith Kumar, watchman at the Madappuram Kaliamman temple, was allegedly assaulted by members of a special police force at a cattle shed behind the temple, leading to his death. This was in connection with a jewellery theft complaint lodged by a devotee on June 27, 2025.
Article Summary: Ajith Kumar, watchman at the Madappuram Kaliamman temple, was allegedly assaulted by members of a special police force at a cattle shed behind the temple, leading to his death. This was in connection with a jewellery theft complaint lodged by a devotee on June 27, 2025.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu shop owner arrested over banner showing Lord Ganesha eating biryani
Article Text:
Based on the complaint, the Tirunelveli city police commenced an inquiry and arrested Jeyanth





MADURAI: Tirunelveli city police on Saturday arrested a biryani shop owner on allegations that a banner depicted Lord Ganesha eating biryani.According to the complainant, Selvaraj, 42, of Narasinganallur, alleged that he had noticed that the banner outside the ‘Dindigul Kalyana Biryani’ shop showed Lord Ganesha eating biryani.He also alleged that the banner was put up with an intention to insult the religious sentiments of Hindus.Based on the complaint, Tirunelveli city police began an inquiry and arrested Jeyanth, 30, of KTC Nagar.He was arrested under Section 299 of the BNS for allegedly committing deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings.
Article Summary: Tirunelveli city police arrested Jeyanth, 30, of KTC Nagar. He was arrested under Section 299 of the BNS for allegedly committing deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings. Selvaraj, 42, of Narasinganallur, alleged that the banner outside the ‘Dindigul Kalyana Biryani’ shop showed Lord Ganesha eating biryani.

Article Title: Kerala HC grants pre-arrest bail to woman accused of throwing her newborn out of hospital window
Article Text:
Kochi:





The high court has granted pre-arrest bail to a 20-year-old unmarried woman from Alappuzha in a case accusing her of throwing her newborn baby through the window of a hospital at Haripad.A bench of Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the accused’s pre-arrest bail petition and directed that she be released on bail in the event of her arrest upon execution of a bond of Rs 1 lakh with two solvent sureties.The prosecution case was that on May 25, while she was admitted to the Taluk Headquarters Hospital, Haripad, she gave birth to a child. In order to avoid the situation arising from the birth of the baby, as she was unmarried, she allegedly threw the baby through the window of the bathroom attached to the hospital room. However, the baby was rescued by the swift intervention of the hospital’s night-duty medical team.According to the petitioner, she was innocent and had been falsely implicated in the crime. The prosecution opposed the petition, contending that her release on bail at this stage would affect the course of the investigation. However, the court observed that there was nothing on record to suggest that the alleged act was committed with an intention to cause the death of the child. Noting that the investigation was almost over and that custodial interrogation of the petitioner was not necessary, the court allowed the petition.
Article Summary: 20-year-old unmarried woman from Alappuzha accused of throwing her newborn baby through the window of a hospital at Haripad. The baby was rescued by the swift intervention of the hospital’s night-duty medical team. According to the petitioner, she was innocent and had been falsely implicated in the crime.

Article Title: GST officials impersonated to dupe establishments; two arrested
Article Text:
Idukki:





The Idukki cybercrime police have arrested two men for allegedly duping various establishments by impersonating GST department officials. The arrested are Johnson E M, 36, of Kunnathunad, Ernakulam, and Anoop P A, 41, of Chettinada, Kodanad.According to the police, the accused contacted various establishments on the phone and allegedly demanded money citing various requirements and misused the name and official designation of the GST department. The fraud was allegedly carried out between May 1 and Aug 7. After a case was registered, the accused went into hiding. A scientific investigation subsequently traced them to the Kozhikode area.The investigation was conducted under the directive of Idukki district police chief A Naseem, with the assistance of the cyber cell. The information collected from various telecom service providers and banks was used to track the accused. They were taken into custody with the assistance of Kodanad Police. The arrest was made by a team led by cybercrime police station inspector Santhosh Sajeev and comprising SIs Anilkumar and Titus, ASI Santhosh Varghese and civil police officers Sandeep, Prathyush, Kiran and Binu.
Article Summary: Idukki cybercrime police have arrested two men for allegedly duping various establishments by impersonating GST department officials. The arrested are Johnson E M, 36, of Kunnathunad, Ernakulam, and Anoop P A, 41, of Chettinada, Kodanad. The fraud was allegedly carried out between May 1 and Aug 7.

Article Title: CMRL ex-official reportedly retracts statement that led to ED report against Pinarayi
Article Text:
Pinarayi Vijayan

Kochi

:





Details have emerged that a former official of Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) has retracted statements he had given to enforcement directorate (ED). The agency has been had relied on them while recommending an FIR against leader of the opposition Pinarayi Vijayan in the Exalogic–CMRL monthly pay-off case.P Suresh Kumar, former chief financial officer and chief general manager of CMRL, submitted the retraction statement to ED directorate in New Delhi on May 15, 2024, alleging intimidation and pressure during questioning by officers of the agency’s Kochi office.In a mail to CMRL on the same day, Kumar said he had felt intimidated while providing statements and clarifications during interrogation. He has since resigned from the company.Incidentally, K S Suresh Kumar, the current chief general manager of CMRL had also submitted a similarly worded retraction statement on May 15, 2024.ED, in a report sent to the state police chief this month, sought registration of a separate FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act and other laws against Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband, former PWD minister, P A Mohamed Riyas.The agency alleged that Vijayan received Rs 3.28 crore through his daughter and accused Riyas of receiving bribes and transferring funds to Dubai through Veena and his associates.
Article Summary: P Suresh Kumar, former chief financial officer and chief general manager of Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) has retracted statements he had given to enforcement directorate. The agency has been had relied on them while recommending an FIR against leader of the opposition Pinarayi Vijayan in the Exalogic–CMRL monthly pay-off case.

Article Title: Two held with 25.36g MDMA in Njarackal
Article Text:
Kochi:





Two men were arrested with 25.36g of MDMA during a drug raid in Njarackal on Wednesday.The arrested are Jithin, 26, of Elamkunnapuzha, and Salih, 32, of Nayarambalam. They were arrested by the rural district Dansaf team, a special investigation team led by Munambam DSP and Njarackal police.Based on a tip-off received by district police chief K S Sudarshan, the police searched the suspects’ house and recovered 15g of MDMA from Jithin’s house and 10.36g from Salih’s house. The drugs were allegedly concealed among clothes.According to the police, the accused had brought the drugs from Bengaluru for sale in the beach areas of Vypeen and Cherai. Police said the two had been under surveillance for some time.Man arrested for theft at MLA’s house: A 24-year-old man from West Bengal was arrested within hours of allegedly stealing wiring cables worth around Rs 50,000 from the under construction house of Muvattupuzha MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan.The arrested is Bishnu Mondal of Murshidabad. He was taken into custody from Kochangadi area of Muvattupuzha.The accused allegedly cut and stole the wiring cables before fleeing.The investigation team led by Kalloorkkad circle inspector Cibi Thomas identified the accused after scientifically examining footage from more than 25 cameras in Pothanikkad and the bus stand area.Police said the accused had been staying in a room during the day and going out in the evening to commit thefts. He allegedly targeted houses under construction.The accused had been released from jail around one-and-a-half months ago after serving a sentence in a case registered by Muvattupuzha police.He had previously been jailed in connection with the theft of generator cables from Kavile, copper wires from a BSNL building in Muvattupuzha and another theft case.Police said the accused was allegedly stealing to buy narcotic substances and maintain a luxurious lifestyle.
Article Summary: Jithin, 26, of Elamkunnapuzha, and Salih, 32, of Nayarambalam, arrested. Police recovered 15g of MDMA from Jithin's house and 10.36g from Salih’s house. The drugs were allegedly concealed among clothes.
